Construct and Modify Parameter Transformations

Source: R/parameters.R
define.Rd

Build, change and branch the symbolic transformations that P() turns into a parfn.

  • define() sets the entry named by the left-hand side of expr to the right-hand side, adding it if missing.

  • insert() replaces the left-hand side by the right-hand side wherever it occurs in the expressions.

  • branch() copies trafo once per condition and keeps table as attribute tree.

Usage

define(trafo, expr, ..., conditionMatch = NULL)

insert(trafo, expr, ..., conditionMatch = NULL)

branch(
  trafo,
  table = NULL,
  conditions = rownames(table),
  apply = c("nothing", "insert", "define")
)

Arguments

trafo

Named character or eqnvec, or a list of those named by condition as branch() returns it. NULL starts a new one.

expr

"lhs <- rhs" string. The symbols in it are replaced by the arguments in ... of the same name; see repar(). For insert() on a branched transformation also one or several effect formulas, e.g. cl ~ wt + (1 | ID), which replace the symbol by a linear predictor over the columns of the branch table with fixed and random effects; see randomEffects(). Named arguments in ... are then placeholders of the formulas, insert(trafo, x ~ 1 + (1 | ID), x = c("ka", "cl")). A substitution or a second effect formula for a symbol that has an effect formula is an error: set the scale of a symbol before adding effects.

...

Named vectors replacing the symbols of expr of the same name, one substitution per element. They are evaluated per condition, with the columns of attr(trafo, "tree"), .currentTrafo (the transformation of the condition) and .currentSymbols (the symbols of that transformation) in scope. An unnamed logical argument of insert() selects the conditions where it is TRUE. Next to effect formulas they are more formulas and placeholders, evaluated once in the calling environment.

conditionMatch

Regular expression; only the conditions whose names match are changed. Default NULL, all. Needs the tree of a transformation built by branch().

table

data.frame with one row per condition, row names the conditions. Kept as attribute tree; the columns can be read in ... by name.

conditions

Condition names; default rownames(table).

apply

One of "nothing" (default), "insert" and "define": what is done with every non-missing entry table[condition, column], with the column name as left-hand side and the entry as right-hand side. Columns named condition or conditions are skipped.

Value

Same shape as trafo, or a list named by condition for branch().

See also

repar(), P()

Examples

## Identity for four parameters, then log parameters
trafo <- define(NULL, "x <- x", x = c("A", "B", "k1", "k2"))
trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = .currentSymbols)
trafo
#> Idx Inner <- Outer
#>   1     A <- exp(A)
#>   2     B <- exp(B)
#>   3    k1 <- exp(k1)
#>   4    k2 <- exp(k2)

## Replace k1 and k2 by expressions, fix B
trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- y", x = c("k1", "k2"), y = c("q1 + q2", "q1 - q2"))
trafo <- define(trafo, "B <- 0")
trafo
#> Idx Inner <- Outer
#>   1     A <- exp(A)
#>   2     B <- 0
#>   3    k1 <- exp(q1+q2)
#>   4    k2 <- exp(q1-q2)

## One branch per condition; the non-missing table entries are inserted
conditions <- data.frame(dose = c(1, 10), q2 = c(NA, "q2_high"),
                         row.names = c("low", "high"))
trafoL <- branch(trafo, table = conditions, apply = "insert")

## Condition-specific changes, selected by name or read off the table
trafoL <- insert(trafoL, "x <- 2*x", x = "q1", conditionMatch = "^high")
trafoL <- define(trafoL, "A <- dose", dose = dose)
trafoL
#> $low
#> Idx Inner <- Outer
#>   1     A <- 1
#>   2     B <- 0
#>   3    k1 <- exp(q1+q2)
#>   4    k2 <- exp(q1-q2)
#> 
#> $high
#> Idx Inner <- Outer
#>   1     A <- 10
#>   2     B <- 0
#>   3    k1 <- exp((2*q1)+q2_high)
#>   4    k2 <- exp((2*q1)-q2_high)
#> 
#> attr(,"tree")
#>      dose      q2
#> low     1    <NA>
#> high   10 q2_high
